sentences.text:
Heard Shri Amol Kumar Srivastava, the learned counsel for the applicants and Sri Diwaker Singh,
learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed for quashing of impugned summoning order dated 25.10.2019 and charge sheet dated 14.04.2018 as well as entire proceeding of Criminal Case No. 89699 of 2019, State Vs. Sunil Kumar and another, arising out of F.I.R. No. 612 of 2017,
under Sections 498A, 147, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Sunil Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. Thru.Prin.Secy. Home And ... on 16 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54247528/
1 Station Thakurganj, District Lucknow pending in the court of learned Special Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, C.B.I. (A.P.), Lucknow.
Learned counsel for the applicants submits that due to financial constraints the applicants could not deposit the aforesaid amount within time and prays that some time may be granted to them for depositing the said amount.
Learned A.G.A. submits that this Court vide order dated 24.01.2023, while referring the matter to the Mediation Centre of this Court directed the applicants to deposit Rs. 25,000/- within three weeks from the date of order and an interim protection was granted to the applicants.

entities.text: Special Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, C.B.I. (A.P.), Lucknow
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Now about four months have elapsed and no money has been deposited by the applicants before the Mediation Centre in compliance of the aforesaid order.

It appears that applicants are not interested to deposit the said amount and they are adopting delaying tactics by not depositing the money as directed earlier and are enjoying fruits of interim protection.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties, perused the order dated 24.01.2023 as well the affidavit filed in support of the present application for extension of time.
The present application has been filed after a lapse of four months, whereas the applicants were granted only three weeks time to deposit the aforesaid amount.
No justified reason has been given in the affidavit filed in support of the present application for extending time further.
The present application has been filed on behalf of applicants only with intention to delay the proceedings initiated against them.
The applicants have failed to show their bonafide regarding non compliance of the order dated 24.01.2023 passed by this Court.
It appears that they are simply lingering on the matter in the garb of the aforesaid order dated 24.01.2023.
The present application (C.M.Application No. 01/2023) is misconceived and is accordingly rejected.
Consequently, the present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is also dismissed.
